items.x_text:
XCPE botnet: Google says 1.3M+ Android TV boxes shipped with a firmware backdoor and attributes it with "high confidence" to maker Videostrong. Access was sold for ad fraud and proxies. Videostrong is now banned from certified Android.

#Botnet #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
1.3 million TV boxes. The backdoor was in the firmware. 📺

What Google disrupted (via Help Net Security, 2 Nov):
→ The XCPE botnet enrolled more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes
→ Google's Threat Intelligence Group attributes it with "high confidence" to Videostrong Technology, which made many of the boxes
→ Access was sold to criminal affiliates: hidden ad views, residential proxies through victims' home connections, account theft, more malware
→ It reinstalls from a protected partition after a reboot and disables Play Protect checks
→ Google took down the servers, banned Videostrong from certified Android, and says cutting the affiliates' domains cuts access to at least 10 million more infected devices

What to do: buy only certified Android TV devices, keep cheap streaming boxes, signage and IoT off your main network, and replace a box you suspect rather than trying to clean it.

cover.hook: 2,400+ banks and credit unions. Their lending app went dark.
cover.sub: Abrigo switched off Sageworks after "irregular activity". Breach not confirmed.

slides.title: What happened
slides.body: On Friday 30 Oct, Abrigo detected suspicious activity and disabled its Sageworks app at about 11:25 a.m. ET. The outage ran through the weekend. Its words: "We identified irregular activity in our environment."

slides.label: entities Abrigo says it serves
slides.note: Mostly US community banks and credit unions (BleepingComputer)

slides.title: Where it stands
slides.body: By 2 Nov most of Sageworks was back. Borrower-facing features (Online Portal Now, Sageworks Analyst, Sageworks API) were still down. Abrigo hasn't said if it was a breach or a technical issue.

slides.title: Why it matters
slides.body: Sageworks holds loan applications and borrower financials. When a shared vendor goes dark, thousands of lenders lose a tool at once. Some researchers advise Sageworks customers to rotate their API keys.

slides.title: Do this week
items: Rotate API keys and tokens shared with the vendor
Ask the vendor for a written incident update
Check your manual fallback for loan processing
Watch logs for odd API calls from vendor IPs

items.question: If your lending platform vanished on a Friday, how long could you keep processing loans?

What happened (AP and Al Jazeera, 2 Nov):
→ Overnight, fridges and freezers in supermarkets were changed to 50°C (122°F) in apparent cyberattacks
→ Reported in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Luxembourg and Sweden: ICA, Coop, Delhaize, Carrefour, Spar and SuperValu stores among them
→ Carrefour Belgium: 15 of 700+ stores. SuperValu: a "cyber incident" at 13 of 223 stores
→ Estonian supplier Kitman Coldtech says attackers reached a computer controlling refrigeration at one client
→ Last month hundreds of French supermarkets were hit the same way. No group has claimed either wave

What to do this week: find every refrigeration, HVAC and building controller reachable from the internet, put remote access behind a VPN with MFA, change default passwords, and alert on any setpoint change. Sweden's cyber centre says many exposed OT devices need updates or patches.

cover.hook: Saved your card at checkout? At Revolve, that's what was taken.
cover.sub: Names, contact details, card numbers and expiry dates, per the retailer's SEC filing.

slides.title: What Revolve disclosed
slides.body: In an 8-K filed 29 Oct, the online fashion retailer said an unauthorized actor may have obtained the name, contact information, card number and expiry date of customers who saved payment info in their accounts.

slides.label: Texas residents affected
slides.note: Per Texas regulators (The Record). Vermont: 1,328. Revolve hasn't given a total.

slides.title: How
slides.body: Revolve says the data may have been obtained "through automated means". It hasn't said when the attack happened or how attackers got in. It notified federal law enforcement and hired outside experts.

slides.title: Why it matters
slides.body: Saved cards are convenience for customers and a target for attackers. Revolve says there was no operational disruption, so the first sign for customers may be fraud on their statements.

slides.title: Do this week
items: Revolve customer? Watch card statements, ask for a new card
Tokenise saved cards; never store raw PANs
Rate-limit and alert on bulk account data reads
Re-check bot defences on account pages

items.question: Do you save your card on shopping sites, or type it in every time?

items.ig_caption:
Saved your card at checkout? At Revolve, that's what was taken. 💳

What we know:
→ Online fashion retailer Revolve told the SEC (8-K, 29 Oct) that an unauthorized actor accessed some of its systems
→ Data at risk: name, contact information, payment card number and expiry date of customers who saved cards in their accounts
→ Revolve says the data may have been obtained "through automated means"
→ Texas regulators were told 127,200 residents are affected; Vermont 1,328. No total yet
→ Revolve notified federal law enforcement and says it expects no material impact

What to do: if you shop at Revolve, watch your card statements and ask your bank for a new card. If you run a store: tokenise saved cards, rate-limit bulk reads of account data, and alert on them.

What IBM's Langflow bulletin says (via The Hacker News, 2 Nov):
→ CVE-2026-93680: authentication bypass, CVSS 9.8, no account needed
→ CVE-2026-110186: arbitrary code execution via the MCP tool path, CVSS 9.8, no account needed
→ CVE-2026-110193 (8.8): a low-privileged user can get the Agentic Assistant to produce code that runs OS commands
→ Every release from 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 is affected; 1.13.0 is the only fix, with no workaround
→ A public Metasploit module exists for CVE-2026-93680. No in-the-wild attacks reported so far

What to do this week: back up the database, secret key and uploaded files, then upgrade to Langflow 1.13.0. If you rely on auto-login, set up password sign-in first (1.13 turns it off by default). Keep Langflow off the public internet.
